LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: RECIPE

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do you write clear instructions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify components of a recipe for information
2. write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning
3. enjoy exploring various ways of preparing foods for cultural appreciation

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe

Teach
• Focus skill: identify components of a recipe for information.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you write clear instructions?
2. what went well and why?
3. what did not go well and why?
4. what can be done differently next time?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
